purpose: AWA's authoritative declaration that the SYSTEM-WIDE operator egress gate is ACTIVE (flipped from spec): all seven PM-facing surfaces are proven to contain ZERO Tier A/B/C banned terms and to express honest confidence, enforced by named tests inside AWA's router-independent `make verify`. This is the AWA side of the `egress` constitution machine-check; the router-side byte-flip in intent-constitution/v1 is the cross-repo counterpart (see constitution_check + consumer/router-pin.json).

single_source_of_truth.note: One matcher + one term snapshot reused by every surface's test, so the banned-term set cannot drift per-surface. The seam test proves this snapshot is a superset of the router's authoritative Tier A/B tiers and that the two matchers agree.

banned_tiers.tier_a_mechanism: lease, worktree, common-dir, kernel, engine, guard, mode, disposition, heartbeat, archive-protect, bundle, quarantine ref, MCP, hook, receipt, flags (+ AWA locals)
banned_tiers.tier_b_git_workflow: branch, commit, push, pull, merge, rebase, PR, main/origin, detached, dirty, ahead/behind, orphan, HEAD
banned_tiers.tier_c_on_disk_leakers: awa_mode_set/awa_guard_shell/awa_lease_read, --bundle/--force/--path, 'mutating command', 'primary checkout', 'policy-check: OK', 'WAL mode', 'Orphan AWA branches'

matching_rule: Word/phrase-bounded. Naturally-lowercase terms match case-INsensitively; all-caps acronyms (PR/MCP/HEAD) match case-SENSITIVELY so they do not collide with ordinary English. Mirrors the router matcher exactly.
bite_proof: Non-tautological: every surface test asserts the REAL rendered output is clean, THEN re-scans that same output with one banned term injected into a real string and REQUIRES a hit (see assertCleanAndBites). Reintroducing a banned term on ANY surface turns the gate red.

surfaces.render_path: kernel/hooks/worktree-guard.sh permission.user_message (deny + ask paths), driven end-to-end
dashboard/seed.canvas.tsx PM_COPY block + dashboard/emitter.py plain_* fields (real emit)
engine/mcp_server.py consent_prompt() — plain intent, never a tool name
consumer/translators.py render_timeline() over the real afterFileEdit detection receipt

honest_confidence.requirement: Every PM-facing status names what it checked AND what it could not (checked/not_checked); no bare pill implies an unauditable guarantee; a partially-built protection names its hole in plain words.

mcp_consent.requirement: Approval labels state plain intent (e.g. 'Temporarily stop protecting this repo?'), never a tool name or mechanism term.

constitution_check.name: egress_zero_banned_terms
constitution_check.router_authoritative_test_id: tests.test_deferred_spec.TestDeferredSpec.test_spec_egress_zero_banned_terms (router repoints this off test_deferred_spec to its active egress test when it flips)
constitution_check.cross_repo_flip: The byte-flip of machine_checks.egress_zero_banned_terms spec->active in KleinPerkins/intent-router intent-constitution.v1.json is the cross-repo counterpart to this AWA-side declaration, and is done in the router's own repo (out of scope for AWA's single PR). AWA cannot write the router repo; the co-installed CI seam job (engine/tests/test_consumer_seam.py::TestRouterSeam::test_constitution_egress_check_active_if_declared) reads the real key + its `status` and enforces `active` when the router declares that machine-check, and consumer/router-pin.json records the expectation. AWA's side is active NOW and enforced by `make verify` via the surface tests above (router-uninstalled); the router still declares `spec`, so its flip PR is the remaining cross-repo step and the seam job (once credentialed) stays RED until it lands.
